entities.name: Alphabet Inc.
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
Alphabet Inc. is an American multinational technology conglomerate created in 2015 as the parent company of Google and its various subsidiaries. Google itself was founded in 1998 by Larry Page and Sergey Brin at Stanford University, with the mission of organizing the world's information and making it universally accessible.

Google's PageRank search algorithm revolutionized the internet by ranking web pages by relevance and authority rather than simple keyword matching, quickly dominating global search. Its advertising platform, AdWords (now Google Ads), created the dominant model for digital advertising that funded the free web. Gmail, Google Maps, YouTube, Chrome, and Android each became essential global infrastructure touching billions of lives daily.

Alphabet's Waymo division leads autonomous vehicle research, DeepMind pioneered artificial intelligence with AlphaGo and protein-folding breakthroughs, and Google Cloud competes in the global cloud market. By controlling search, email, mapping, mobile OS, and video, Alphabet became arguably the most significant information company in history, processing over 8.5 billion search queries per day.
